title: It’s time to keep our promise to protect Antarctica
gist: John Kerry urges governments meeting at CCAMLR in Hobart to agree krill fishery management, the Domain 1 marine protected area and a 2030 timetable for a circum-Antarctic MPA network. He argues Antarctica is a rare place where multilateral cooperation can still work.

insights.claim: Kerry says a Hobart CCAMLR breakthrough requires agreement on three things: science-based krill fishery management, the Chile/Argentina Domain 1 Antarctic Peninsula MPA, and a firm timetable for a full MPA network by 2030.
insights.speaker: John Kerry
insights.so_what: The Hobart outcome is a binary catalyst for krill-fishing restrictions and Southern Ocean protection.

insights.claim: Agreeing the proposals already on the table plus existing protections would protect over a quarter of the Southern Ocean.
insights.speaker: John Kerry
insights.so_what: Quantifies the upside of the current negotiating package.
insights.locator: Just agreeing to the proposals already on the table

insights.claim: Krill management should spread catches across regions and seasons rather than concentrating fishing pressure in sensitive areas and times.
insights.speaker: John Kerry
insights.so_what: Likely regulatory direction for the krill industry: spatial and seasonal catch limits.

insights.claim: Two years ago governments allowed spatial controls on krill fishing to expire, so industrial vessels can concentrate catch in feeding grounds that penguins, seals and whales depend on.
insights.speaker: John Kerry
insights.so_what: The regulatory gap raises ecological and reputational risk for krill operators until controls are restored.
insights.locator: Two years ago, governments allowed spatial controls

insights.claim: Industry is now engaging constructively at the table, partly thanks to King Charles III bringing governments, scientists, industry and civil society together.
insights.speaker: John Kerry
insights.so_what: Industry buy-in raises the odds that restrictions pass.
insights.locator: Industry is now at the table in a new and constructive way

insights.claim: Just over 10 per cent of the ocean is protected against a 2022 pledge to protect 30 per cent of land and ocean by 2030, so coverage must triple in four years.
insights.speaker: John Kerry
insights.so_what: The gap implies a large pipeline of future MPA designations and fishing-access restrictions.
insights.locator: just over 10 per cent of the ocean is protected

insights.claim: The Ross Sea Region MPA negotiated in 2016, about 1.55 million sq km, was then the largest ocean conservation area, yet no new Antarctic protections have been created in the decade since.
insights.speaker: John Kerry
insights.so_what: Shows how great-power divisions have stalled CCAMLR consensus, so base rates for new MPAs are low.
insights.locator: Ross Sea Region Marine Protected Area
